guard: the channel-membership feature smoke provisions each unique space on its own broker and uses a valid custom actor id
why: Each scenario invents a unique space. Before this repair, no code created that space's streams, so every endpoint failed with stream not found and none of the feature assertions ran.

The stale lossy-id fixture also used a dotted actor id that the current principal grammar deliberately rejects. Named preconditions keep both harness requirements legible instead of letting setup throws masquerade as product failures.

mutations.name: restore the rejected dotted actor fixture
mutations.expectRed: E: custom id follows the current owner/actor token grammar
mutations.cell: E: custom id follows the current owner/actor token grammar
